question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key locations showing Clive's rising influence in Madras and Carnatic]
options: Fort St. George (Madras) — Clive's base of operations and headquarters where his influence began to rise
Fort St. David (Cuddalore) — site where Clive was appointed as deputy governor after returning to India
Pondicherry — French headquarters captured by Clive in 1754, ending French power before Plassey
Gheriah (Vijaydurg) — pirate stronghold on the western coast captured by Clive and Admiral Watson in 1756
wrong_fact: Pondicherry was never captured by Clive in 1754. French control over Pondicherry remained intact until it was captured much later in 1761 by Eyre Coote during the Third Carnatic War.
explanation: Clive's rise to prominence began at Fort St. George and Fort St. David. In 1756, prior to going to Bengal, Clive and Admiral Watson destroyed the Maratha pirate stronghold of Gheriah (Vijaydurg) on the western coast. Pondicherry remained the French headquarters throughout the Second Carnatic War and was not captured by Clive in 1754.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Clive's regional military expeditions that raised his standing before 1756]
options: Expedition to Devikottai (1749) — British attack on a fort near the Coleroon River mouth in Tanjore
Capture of Covelong (1752) — Clive led a force of raw recruits to seize a French fort south of Madras
Capture of Chingleput (1752) — Clive captured the fort inland to secure Madras from French incursions
Expedition to Surat (1755) — Clive's land march across central India to establish British control in Gujarat
wrong_fact: Clive never led an expedition to Surat or marched across central India to Gujarat in 1755. He arrived back in India in late 1755 at Bombay, from where he led the joint expedition to Gheriah (Vijaydurg) on the Konkan coast.
explanation: Clive's early military exploits that earned him fame included the Devikottai expedition (1749) and the capture of Covelong and Chingleput (1752) near Madras. He returned from England in late 1755, arriving in Bombay, and from there he launched an expedition against Gheriah (1756) on the western coast. He did not march to Surat or Gujarat.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical redistribution of European power showing Clive's rising influence]
options: Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) — signed in Pondicherry, resulting in the recall of Dupleix and mutual return of territories
Deccan region — French forces under Bussy remained entrenched at Hyderabad, limiting British influence there
Bombay Coast — Clive's destruction of Gheriah cleared Maratha naval power, raising British prestige on the west coast
Bengal Presidency — Clive was appointed Governor of Calcutta in 1753, establishing his dominance in northeastern India
wrong_fact: Clive was not appointed Governor of Calcutta (Bengal) in 1753. He was in England from 1753 to 1755, and only went to Bengal in late 1756 after the fall of Calcutta to Siraj-ud-Daulah.
explanation: The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) ended the Second Carnatic War, resulting in Dupleix's recall. French General Bussy maintained influence in Hyderabad. Clive's victory at Gheriah in early 1756 increased British influence on the western coast. Clive did not become governor of Calcutta in 1753; he was in England, and only sailed to Bengal in late 1756 to recapture Calcutta.
